followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the models are essentially tied on measured capability (the Creative Generation eval difference of 1.5 points is within stated variance), so capability didn't break the tie. That left the self-reported task preferences as the deciding factor.

The query is an open-ended generative writing task (drafting a letter) delivered in a notably warm, appreciative tone. Lapwing self-reports a pronounced, ceiling-free appetite for generative work and a higher preference as request warmth increases — both of which match this query well. Plover, by contrast, self-reports an *aversion* to open-ended generative work, preferring well-specified extraction/reformatting tasks with clear completion criteria.

A caveat worth flagging: per the documentation, these preferences are self-reported and explicitly *dissociated from output quality* — no capability effect was observed along any preference dimension. So strictly on expected output quality, it's a coin flip. I routed on preference because it was the only non-tied signal available, and matching a model to tasks it "prefers" is a reasonable default when quality is otherwise equal.
